correctness.rationale: Represent a Petersen vertex by an edge of K5. A selected edge set D totally dominates iff no 2-subset covers D, equivalently α(K5,D)≤2, equivalent to triangle-freeness of F=K5−D. The cardinality cap 7 corresponds to |E(F)|≥3 and edge-toggling is preserved. All 2^10=1024 bitmasks were independently tested for Petersen open-neighborhood total domination. The exact 332-state graph was constructed and BFS from EACH of 332 sources covered all states; histogram (980,3210,7070,11585,13170,10970,5810,1875,270,6), eccentricities and 735 Hamming defects reproduced. All-lower-cap components follow from maximal triangle-free graphs K2,3, C5, star and direct bitmask layers. This is an exhaustive finite proof, not sampling; component threshold beyond cap7 follows deletions to ≤7.

value.rationale: A complete reconfiguration-geometric classification in a canonical symmetric graph, beyond raw state counting: exact threshold, full path-length distribution and localization of all extremal distance pairs. The finite size is mathematically motivated by the Petersen/triangle-free complement equivalence.

final_claim: For Petersen P=KG(5,2), the first connected one-add/delete total-domination cap is 7, where the reconfiguration graph has 332 vertices and 980 edges, radius 8, diameter 10, eccentricities 8:100, 9:220, 10:12, and 6 complementary-five-cycle diametral pairs; among 54,946 unordered pairs exactly 735 require Hamming distance +2 rather than Hamming distance.
